new.title: See the Yıldırım Bayezid Mosque in Bolu
new.desc: The main mosque of Bolu is attributed to the Ottoman sultan Yıldırım Bayezid, with a first building dated to 1382, and it was rebuilt in the 19th century. Beside it stand the Bayezid bath and the restored 1750 Taşhan caravanserai.
new.tip: Free to enter outside prayer times; modest dress required. The surrounding streets are the old bazaar quarter.
new.q: Yıldırım Beyazıt Camii, Tabaklar, Bolu Merkez, Bolu

new.title: Look into the 1499 Kadı Mosque on İzzet Baysal Street
new.desc: The Kadı Mosque is an Ottoman mosque in the centre of Bolu dated to 1499, standing on the main street named after the local benefactor İzzet Baysal.
new.tip: Pair it with a walk along İzzet Baysal Caddesi and tea in the bazaar. Visit outside prayer times.
new.q: Kadı Camii, İzzet Baysal Caddesi, Bolu Merkez, Bolu

new.title: Browse the Bolu Museum's archaeology and ethnography
new.desc: Founded in 1981, the Bolu Museum shows finds from local excavations alongside ethnographic collections of the region.
new.tip: Allow about an hour. State museums are usually closed on Mondays; check before going.
new.q: Bolu Müzesi, Karamanlı, Bolu Merkez, Bolu

new.title: Steam in the Bayezid Bath, Bolu's 1388 double hammam
new.desc: The Yıldırım Beyazıt Hamamı next to the mosque is a historic double bathhouse dated to 1388, with separate sections for men and women.
new.tip: Check the current men's and women's hours; mornings are quietest.
new.q: Yıldırım Bayezid Hamamı, Büyükcami, Bolu Merkez, Bolu

new.title: Take tea in the restored 1750 Bolu Taşhan
new.desc: The Taşhan is a caravanserai from 1750 next to the Yıldırım Beyazıt Mosque, restored and now run as a café and hotel around its stone courtyard.
new.tip: Go in the afternoon for tea and something sweet; the courtyard is pleasant in dry weather.
new.q: Bolu Taşhan, Tabaklar, Bolu Merkez, Bolu

new.title: Walk around Gölcük Nature Park's crater lake
new.desc: Gölcük is a small volcanic crater lake and nature park about 13 km from Bolu, surrounded by forest and known for its lakeside house photo spot. Entry to the park is free.
new.tip: Best in autumn or spring; mornings are calmer than weekends.
new.q: Gölcük Tabiat Parkı, Bolu Merkez, Bolu

new.title: Circle Lake Abant, Turkey's 48th national park
new.desc: Abant is a landslide-dammed lake at 1,328 m in beech and pine forest; the area was protected as a nature park from 1988 and declared a national park on 10 June 2022. The trail around the shore is roughly 7 km.
new.tip: Come on a weekday in October for the colours, or early in the morning to avoid crowds.
new.q: Abant Gölü Milli Parkı, Mudurnu, Bolu

new.title: Ski or hike the Köroğlu Mountains at Kartalkaya
new.desc: Kartalkaya is a ski resort in the Köroğlu Mountains with 14 trails, 3 chairlifts and a top at 2,255 m; the season runs roughly from late December to March.
new.tip: The Grand Kartal Hotel was destroyed by fire on 21 January 2025; check current resort and hotel status before booking.
new.q: Kartalkaya Kayak Merkezi, Seben, Bolu

new.title: Hike Yedigöller's seven landslide lakes
new.desc: Yedigöller National Park, established in 1965 near Mengen, protects seven landslide lakes at about 900 m: Büyükgöl, Deringöl, Seringöl, Nazlıgöl, Sazlıgöl, İncegöl and Küçükgöl. It is famous for autumn colour.
new.tip: Autumn is busiest; in winter the Bolu road can close and access goes via Yeniçağa and Mengen.
new.q: Yedigöller Millî Parkı, Yığılca, Düzce

new.title: Meet the Chef Statue at the gates of Mengen
new.desc: Mengen is Turkey's cooks' town; its chefs trace back to Ottoman palace kitchens, the first cooking school opened here in 1985, and a statue of a chef marks the town entrance. A cooks' festival is held in the first week of September.
new.tip: The festival in early September is the best time; combine with lunch in town.
new.q: Mengen Aşçı Heykeli, Mengen, Bolu

new.title: Eat Mengen pilavı and Abant kebabı at Mercan-i
new.desc: Mercan-i Restaurant in Bolu's old centre serves local classics: buttered Bolu potatoes, Mengen pilavı and Abant kebabı, which combines chicken and lamb.
new.tip: Order the Mengen pilavı with ayran; lunch is the busy time.
new.q: Mercan-i Restaurant, Özek Sokak No:3, Tabaklar, Bolu

new.title: Eat wood-fired pide at Kral Pide
new.desc: Kral Pide in Karaçayır bakes pide in a wood-fired oven and also cooks daily stews.
new.tip: Come at lunch for the freshest pide; ask which stew is on that day.
new.q: Kral Pide, PTT Caddesi, Karaçayır, Bolu

new.title: Taste hand-rolled gözleme at Kubbealtı
new.desc: Kubbealtı on İzzet Baysal Caddesi specialises in hand-rolled gözleme, both savoury and sweet.
new.tip: Try a cheese or spinach gözleme with tea; a light stop between sights.
new.q: Kubbealtı, İzzet Baysal Caddesi No:108, Bolu

new.title: See the single-dome Yıldırım Bayezid Mosque in Mudurnu
new.desc: Built in 1372 as part of a complex with dervish lodges, a hamam and a madrasa, the mosque is described as the first with a large single dome without columns.
new.tip: Walk on to the 1382 hamam and the Ahilik Museum in the bazaar.
new.q: Yıldırım Bayezid Külliyesi, Mudurnu, Bolu

new.title: Bathe in Mudurnu's working 1382 Yıldırım Bayezid Hamam
new.desc: The Yıldırım Bayezid Hamam in Mudurnu was built in 1382 and is still in use as a Turkish bath with a sauna.
new.tip: Check the men's and women's times; afternoon is quiet.
new.q: Yıldırım Bayezid Hamamı, Mudurnu, Bolu

new.title: Step inside the 27-room Armutçular Mansion
new.desc: Armutçular Mansion in the centre of Mudurnu is a 27-room Ottoman mansion with carved wooden ceilings, in a town whose centre is a protected historic district.
new.tip: Ask locally about opening hours; combine with a stroll through the old streets.
new.q: Armutçular Konağı, Mudurnu, Bolu

new.title: Learn the Ahilik guild tradition at Mudurnu's museum
new.desc: The Mudurnu Ahilik Museum in the bazaar presents the Ahi craft guild tradition and the old trades of the town.
new.tip: Visit before browsing the bazaar's craft shops.
new.q: Mudurnu Ahilik Müzesi, Çarşı, Mudurnu, Bolu

new.title: Start the day with paça çorbası at Kanaat Lokantası
new.desc: Kanaat Lokantası on Bolu Caddesi is one of Mudurnu's oldest lokantas, known for soup-based breakfasts and above all its trotter (paça) soup.
new.tip: Go in the morning; it is also well rated for lunch dishes.
new.q: Kanaat Lokantası, Bolu Caddesi, Seyrancık, Mudurnu, Bolu

new.title: Breakfast in the wooden Hacı Şakirler Konağı
new.desc: Hacı Şakirler Konağı in Mudurnu's Musalla quarter serves a traditional breakfast with village bread, cheeses, eggs and sweet spreads inside a wooden historic house.
new.tip: Book at weekends; the house is on a narrow old street, so walk in.
new.q: Hacı Şakirler Konağı, Musalla Mahallesi, Mudurnu, Bolu

new.title: Soak at Babas Thermal Spa near Mudurnu
new.desc: Babas Kaplıcası is a mineral hot-spring spa about 3 km from Mudurnu with accommodation in a restored Ottoman wooden bathhouse.
new.tip: Call ahead for day entry and bathing sessions.
new.q: Babas Kaplıcası, Gürçam Köyü, Mudurnu, Bolu

new.title: Walk the Akkaya Travertines between Bolu and Mudurnu
new.desc: The Akkaya Travertines are white terraces formed by mineral-rich spring water of more than 20 degrees, on the road between Bolu and Mudurnu.
new.tip: Avoid winter, when snow cuts visibility; wear shoes with grip.
new.q: Akkaya Travertenleri, Mudurnu, Bolu

new.title: Visit Akşemseddin's tomb in Göynük
new.desc: The tomb of the Ottoman scholar and mystic Akşemseddin (1389-1459), spiritual guide of Mehmed the Conqueror, stands in the courtyard of the Gazi Süleyman Paşa Mosque in Göynük. Its walnut sarcophagus carries carved inscriptions.
new.tip: Dress modestly and walk the old streets nearby.
new.q: Akşemseddin Türbesi, Cuma Mahallesi, Göynük, Bolu

new.title: Climb to Göynük's wooden Victory Tower
new.desc: The Zafer Kulesi on the hill above Göynük is a six-sided wooden tower on a stone base, built in 1923 and overlooking the town's Ottoman houses.
new.tip: Climb at dusk for roof views.
new.q: Zafer Kulesi, Göynük, Bolu

new.title: Breakfast with bal-kaymak at Akşemsettinoğlu Konağı
new.desc: A historic konak in Göynük serving a breakfast with honey and clotted cream (bal-kaymak) and gözleme.
new.tip: Reserve at weekends; breakfast is the main draw.
new.q: Akşemsettinoğlu Konağı, Gazi Süleyman Paşa Bulvarı, Yenice, Göynük, Bolu

new.title: Picnic and eat trout at Sünnet Lake near Göynük
new.desc: Sünnet Lake is a landslide lake in forest, now a nature park with trout facilities and a short shore path, near Göynük.
new.tip: Best in summer and autumn.
new.q: Sünnet Gölü Tabiat Parkı, Göynük, Bolu

new.title: See Taraklı's Yunus Paşa Mosque and Ottoman houses
new.desc: Taraklı is a mountain town with more than 100 registered Ottoman houses. At its centre stands the Yunus Paşa Mosque, dated 1517 and attributed to Mimar Sinan.
new.tip: Wander the cobbled lanes; local shops sell wooden combs and spoons.
new.q: Yunus Paşa Camii, Taraklı, Sakarya

new.title: Eat in the Ottoman Kadirler Konağı in Taraklı
new.desc: Kadirler Konağı is a restored Ottoman mansion in Taraklı that now works as a hotel and restaurant.
new.tip: Reserve ahead at weekends.
new.q: Kadirler Konağı, Taraklı, Sakarya

new.title: Peer into the Seben rock houses
new.desc: The Seben Rock Houses are rock-carved dwellings of four to five levels connected by chimney stairs, with crosses and Latin inscriptions suggesting use from Early Christian to Middle Byzantine times.
new.tip: Wear sturdy shoes and bring a torch for the interiors.
new.q: Solaklar Kaya Evleri, Solaklar, Seben, Bolu

new.title: Sit in the Prusias ad Hypium theatre
new.desc: The theatre of Prusias ad Hypium at Konuralp, locally called the Forty Stairs, dates to the Hellenistic period (300-30 BC) and once seated about 10,000; the stage building dates to around 190 AD.
new.tip: Combine with the town museum; afternoon light is best.
new.q: Prusias ad Hypium Antik Tiyatrosu, Konuralp, Düzce

new.title: Visit the Konuralp Museum's mosaics
new.desc: Opened in 2003, the Konuralp Museum holds 6,237 objects including 3,898 coins, a garland sarcophagus and an Orpheus floor mosaic, all linked to Prusias ad Hypium.
new.tip: Check opening days; it sits at the entrance to Konuralp.
new.q: Konuralp Müzesi, Konuralp, Düzce

new.title: Hike to Güzeldere Waterfall in Gölyaka
new.desc: Güzeldere is a waterfall nature park in Gölyaka, with a drop that sources put at about 120 to 135 m, with trails and picnic areas.
new.tip: Go in spring when the flow is highest; paths can be slippery.
new.q: Güzeldere Şelalesi Piknik Alanı, Güzeldere, Gölyaka, Düzce

new.title: Walk to Samandere Waterfall's canyon
new.desc: Samandere is a registered natural monument near Beyköy, about 24 km from Düzce, known for its canyon and old trees.
new.tip: Wear shoes with grip.
new.q: Samandere Şelalesi, Samandere, Düzce

new.title: Watch birds at Efteni Lake
new.desc: Efteni (Melen) Lake in Gölyaka is a wetland bird sanctuary with about 150 bird species.
new.tip: Bring binoculars; spring and autumn migration are best.
new.q: Efteni Gölü, Gölyaka, Düzce

new.title: Climb to the Genoese castle above Akçakoca
new.desc: The Ceneviz Kalesi is a small ruined Genoese castle on the headland by Akçakoca's castle beach; the Genoese built it to protect trade routes on the Black Sea coast.
new.tip: Combine with the beach below; sunset is good.
new.q: Ceneviz Kalesi, Akçakoca, Düzce

new.title: Swim at Çuhallı Beach in Akçakoca
new.desc: Çuhallı is the long sandy Blue Flag beach by Akçakoca town on the western Black Sea.
new.tip: Swim in July and August.
new.q: Çuhallı Plajı, Akçakoca, Düzce

new.title: Explore Fakıllı Cave near Akçakoca
new.desc: Fakıllı Cave is a stalactite cave about 350 m of which is open to visitors.
new.tip: Wear shoes with grip; the cave is cool and damp.
new.q: Fakıllı Mağarası, Akçakoca, Düzce

new.title: Eat su böreği at Börekçi İsmet Usta
new.desc: Tarihi Börekçi İsmet Usta has been baking börek in Düzce since 1972, known for su böreği and Boşnak böreği.
new.tip: Go in the morning when the börek is fresh.
new.q: Tarihi Börekçi İsmet Usta, Namık Kemal Sokak 42/A, Kültür, Düzce

new.title: Cross the Justinian Bridge (Beşköprü)
new.desc: The Sangarius Bridge near Adapazarı, called Beşköprü, was built by Emperor Justinian in 533 AD on the Byzantine military road east from Constantinople.
new.tip: Easiest by car; the area is quiet.
new.q: Justinianus Köprüsü (Beşköprü), Sakarya

new.title: See the Sakarya Museum in Atatürk's old house
new.desc: The Sakarya Museum is also known as Atatürk Evi; Atatürk met his mother here in 1922. Entry is free and it is closed on Mondays.
new.tip: Pair with the Uzun Çarşı.
new.q: Sakarya Müzesi, Adapazarı, Sakarya

new.title: Walk the Ottoman-era Uzun Çarşı of Adapazarı
new.desc: The Tarihi Uzun Çarşı is an Ottoman-era bazaar still used for trade, with the Orta Camii of 1752 inside it.
new.tip: Visit on a weekday morning.
new.q: Uzun Çarşı Sokağı, Cumhuriyet, Adapazarı, Sakarya

new.title: Eat ıslama köfte at Köfteci Mustafa
new.desc: Köfteci Mustafa near Yeni Cami, founded in 1912, is credited with the first ıslama köfte, a Sakarya dish of day-old bread soaked in bone broth and served with grilled meatballs; it has a geographical indication.
new.tip: Go at lunch and order the ıslama köfte.
new.q: Köfteci Mustafa, Yeni Cami Mahallesi, Sakarya Caddesi 12, Adapazarı, Sakarya

new.title: Walk around Poyrazlar Lake Nature Park
new.desc: Poyrazlar Lake nature park is about 8 km north of Adapazarı; 154 bird species have been recorded.
new.tip: Bring binoculars.
new.q: Poyrazlar Gölü Tabiat Parkı, Adapazarı, Sakarya

new.title: Walk the Acarlar floodplain forest boardwalk
new.desc: Acarlar Longozu is described as Turkey's largest unbroken floodplain forest, with a walking platform and birdwatching.
new.tip: Go in spring; bring insect repellent.
new.q: Acarlar Longozu, Karasu, Sakarya

new.title: Soak at the Kuzuluk thermal springs
new.desc: Kuzuluk Kaplıcaları is a thermal spa area in Sakarya's Akyazı.
new.tip: Check the facility hours.
new.q: Kuzuluk Kaplıcaları, Kuzuluk, Akyazı, Sakarya
